message:
Structural Dynamicist and the Manager, the device holds maximum comfort because 1.9 Hz sits in the lively walking range and the limit is peak vertical acceleration below 0.700 m/s2, about 0.0714 g, per the maximum comfort band described in the Analysis of Footbridge Comfort Vibrations (E13) and the four-level scale in the A Review of Evaluation Methods of Standards for Structural Vibration Serviceability under Crowd Walking (E2), with 1.90 Hz inside the critical 1.25 to 2.30 Hz vertical range needing a check.

Retrofit and Maintenance Engineer, the device faces three crowd cases that can hit resonance, with single walker at 1.90 Hz, dense stream near 0.600 walkers per square metre, and synchronized walking 1.80 to 2.20 Hz step frequency, where bare single-walker response is about 1.75 m/s2, about 0.178 g like a bouncing floor, per the bare single-ped resonant accel estimate (E22), needing reduction factor 2.50 per the required response reduction factor calculation (E31) and effective damping of several percent against bare near 0.400%.

Under-Deck Integration Designer, the device passes acceptance because the Tuned Mass Damper (TMD), a sprung mass moving out of phase, cuts resonance to damped peak 0.106 m/s2, about 0.0108 g like a still floor, below 0.700 m/s2, with stroke 2.52 mm inside plus-minus 30.0 mm clearance, per the damped response sweep (E32), using 800 kg at 4.00% ratio per the Den Hartog sizing (E11). Ready, because comfort, crowd cases and damped proof are frozen with margin.
